newsitem.title: SWEDEN: S&P assigns "A" corporate rating to Atlas Copco.
newsitem.headline: S&P assigns "A" corporate rating to Atlas Copco.

text.p: U.S. credit ratings agency Standard & Poor's said on Thursday it assigned a corporate credit rating of "A" to Swedish engineering group Atlas Copco AB with a negative outlook.
S&P said in a statement it also affirmed an A-1 short-term rating for Atlas Copco.
"The ratings reflect Atlas Copco's leading market position within areas of operation, relatively stable cash flow generation throughout the business cycle and sound financial policies," S&P said.

It said although Atlas Copco's markets are mature, the industry was favourable, especially for compressors. S&P said that even after the proposed acquisition of Prime Service, compressors will still make up about 40 percent of sales.
"There are relatively few competitors and barriers to entry are high, reflecting technical skills, distribution, service network and brand name," S&P said.

Although the acquisition of Prime Service, financed by debt, will increase leverage and raise net debt to capital to about 35 to 40 percent on a pro forma basis, Atlas Copco should be able to adequately reduce debt given its strong core business.
"Atlas Copco's cash flow and coverage ratios are expected to remain adequate for the rating category," it said.
